title: Dual-Purpose Reused Variables (Lie-to-Reader)
pattern: Reusing an input parameter or a local variable to hold a computed intermediate value that has a semantically different meaning than its original initialization.
why_bad: It constitutes disinformation. The variable name (e.g., `value` or `input_val`) becomes a lie. If a maintainer later attempts to use `value` assuming it contains the raw input, they will introduce silent calculation bugs.
detection: Match parameters declared as mutable (`mut`) that are reassigned values computed from themselves in non-trivial ways.
